newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia rate cut chance 50-50 - CBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia rate cut chance 50-50 - CBA.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) chief executive David Murray said he thought there was an even chance that the Reserve Bank of Australia would cut interest rates this week after its board meeting on Tuesday.
Murray said there were two factors against a cut in rates.

"One is that even though the Reserve Bank meets on Tuesday's it doesn't always change the rate on Tuesday's and the second is that we've not often seen a 25 basis point change in Australia, it's more likely to be 50 basis points change," he told the Nine Network's Business Sunday television programme.
"There's only about 10 basis points written into the market rates at the moment. That's not a reason for them not to come down but at this stage it's even money in my book," he said.
The Reserve Bank last reduced rates by 50 basis points to 7.0 percent on July 31 and meets for its regular board meeting on Tuesday.
A Reuters survey of 32 economists on Friday showed only 10 thought a rate cut in October was a likely or a definite possiblity.
Most of the other economists thought a rate reduction was most likely in November, based on continuing weak employment and low inflation data.
Murray said there were a number of indicators showing a slight upturn in the economy, such as housing activity and some business activity.
